subject: Follow-up: Encryption/KMS options and next steps

Cc: security@fintechco.com, procurement@fintechco.com

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on encryption options

Thanks Marissa — great call today. A few clarifying Qs from our security/infra team about encryption:

1) We need to confirm that data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Are you using TLS 1.2+ and AES-256 at rest?
2) For at-rest keys, can we bring our own key (BYOK) via AWS KMS / GCP KMS? Is there an HSM-backed option?
3) How are key rotations handled and can we audit key use? We need proof for our compliance team.

Can you send a short doc and sample architecture diagram? Also, our procurement team will want to understand the contract-side controls for customer-managed keys.

Thanks,
Sara

Head of Security, FintechCo
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-20T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on encryption options

Hi Sara — thanks for the thoughtful questions and for the time on the call. Recap below and proposed next steps.

Short answers:
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 (fallback to TLS 1.2 where required); mutual TLS available for private deployments.
- At-rest: AES-256 encryption for all hosted data. For Dedicated/Private, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS (BYOK). HSM-backed options via partner integrations or on-prem HSM are available for Private deployments.
- Key rotation & audit: We support automated rotation policies (you can set rotation frequency) and provide key usage logs tied into our audit log stream (Cloud Audit, SIEM integration). We can provide sample log extracts.

Attachments: redwood-kms-options.pdf (summary), redwood-encryption-arch.drawio.png (architecture). Also linking to our security page.

Next steps:
1) Security deep-dive call with our SecOps and your security team — propose Tue 3/23 10am PT.
2) I'll loop in our product engineer (Ben) for KMS configuration details and Neha for procurement redlines.
3) We'll send a short technical note and a DocuSign template for BYOK addendum if needed.

If that all sounds good I can lock in the meeting.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-21T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on encryption options

Sara — quick technical clarifications from my side:

- BYOK flow: We support envelope encryption. Your CMK (Customer Master Key) in AWS KMS/GCP KMS encrypts a data encryption key (DEK) that we use to encrypt model artifacts and persisted request logs. We never export your CMK; the envelope pattern keeps the DEK protected.
- HSM: For Private/on-prem, we can integrate with existing HSMs via PKCS#11 or use cloud HSM (CloudHSM, Cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys) depending on your architecture.
- Logging: All key actions (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) are surfaced in our audit logs. For hosted customers, we provide token-level logging with redaction options; for Dedicated/Private you can send logs to your SIEM.

Attaching our KMS options PDF and a diagram — happy to walk through on the call.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
